findings.message: role() turns a failed or not-yet-present meta read into `null` (`.catch(() => undefined)`; `text()` also returns undefined when the file is absent). It then caches that `null` in `roles` for the life of the mod. 'Could not ask' and 'no agent type' collapse into one value, and the wrong answer is never retried. The subagent's cost is billed to the generic 'subagent' role until the mod reloads. Fix: cache only a successfully parsed agentType. On a failed read or an absent meta, leave the entry uncached so the next refresh asks again. Prune `roles` along with `scans`.
findings.scenario: A refresh fires (tool.call or turn.complete) while `s1/subagents/agent-a1.jsonl` exists but `agent-a1.meta.json` is not written yet, or its read throws once. roles caches null. Later `agent-a1.meta.json` = {"agentType":"code-reviewer"} appears, but every later refresh still shows `by role: main $… · subagent $…` instead of `code-reviewer $…`, until a reload.

findings.message: The new `dash` feature is offered on every host, but specclaw-dash is a Claude Code mod with no Codex manifest. The core `specclaw` plugin, which ships a Codex manifest and the status skill, now tells Codex users to install a plugin that cannot run there. `installed()` cannot find it under Codex either, so the tip always fires. The fix covers Claude Code, the named host, but misses the Codex variant. Fix: suppress the dash tip outside Claude Code (for example, when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset or the host is Codex). Add a test row for that case.
findings.scenario: In a Codex session with a change in `build`, the status skill step 6 runs `specclaw-suggest .specclaw dash`. It prints `Tip: a /dash pane … Install: /plugin install specclaw-dash@chan4lk`, a plugin Codex cannot load.

findings.message: resolveHead is fed by quietText, which maps every read failure to undefined, the same value as a missing file. A loose ref whose read fails falls through to `packed-refs`, which may hold an older sha. The review row then reads 'behind HEAD' instead of unknown. Fix: map only absent files and folders to undefined, and let other read errors turn atHead into null (unknown).

parseFleet re-implements the fleet report validity check from plugins/specclaw-fleet/hooks/core/report.ts:29, and the two copies already disagree: report.ts requires `Array.isArray(doc.rows)` and dash does not. A cross-plugin import is not possible, but the condition should match, with a comment naming report.ts as the source.

DEAREST is a hand-copied literal of the claude-fable-5-1 row, not derived from PRICES. If the table changes, or a dearer model is added, unknown models stop pricing as 'the dearest' as the comment promises. Compute it from PRICES (the max of each column, or the row with the highest input price).

CONTEXT_WINDOW is a fixed 1,000,000 for every model, yet the price table treats the `[1m]` suffix as a variant. A session on a smaller-window model shows a context % that is far too low. Key the window by model, or omit the % for models whose window is not known.

If neither CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR nor HOME is set, `base` becomes the string 'undefined/.claude', and the tokens section shows a 'No Claude Code transcripts' install card instead of an error. Fail with an error when HOME is missing.

The AC-7 read-only check greps only for `$.fs.write` and `$.process`. Any other mutating $.fs call (for example remove, mkdir or rename, if the API has them) passes as 'no write'. Widen the pattern to every non-read $.fs method, or allow-list the read methods (exists, read, list).

The privacy paragraph lists what the scanner keeps (counts, times, ids, model names, session titles, agent types) but omits the git branch. scan.ts stores `gitBranch`, and the pane shows it as the session name fallback. Add branch names to the list.
